title: Hairpin braid join — linking the strips into fabric
subtitle: Group and braid loops from adjacent strips to join them without visible seams
excerpt: The hairpin braid join groups loops from two adjacent hairpin strips and pulls them through each other to lock them together. The groups of interlaced loops form a visible braid pattern between the strips. This is the standard method for assembling hairpin lace fabric from individual strips.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Vol. 2 (1887) — joining hairpin lace strips. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776 — loop-joining in hairpin and tatting work.

glossaryTerms.definition: A method of joining adjacent hairpin lace strips by taking groups of loops from each strip and threading them through each other in sequence. The interlaced loops form a braid that holds the strips together while leaving the outer loops free for the next strip or edge.

heroPrompt: Two hairpin lace strips in pale pink DK yarn joined along one edge, the braided loop join visible as a decorative centre line between the two open strips, close-up.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: The first group of loops from strip 2 being pulled through the first group of loops from strip 1

content.text: links the inner loops of two strips by passing each group of loops through the previous group. The join is visible as a decorative braid and holds without any dc or chain stitching between the strips. Both outer edges remain free for adding more strips or an edging.
Basic braid join (2 loops per group)
Lay both strips parallel, with the inner edges (the edges you want to join) facing each other.
Pick up the first 2 loops from strip 1 (inner edge) on the hook or fingers.
Pull the first 2 loops from strip 2 through the 2 loops from strip 1.
Pull the next 2 loops from strip 1 through the 2 loops now held from strip 2.
Continue alternating: 2 from strip 2 through the held strip-1 loops, then 2 from strip 1 through the held strip-2 loops. The braid forms as you progress.
At the end, secure the final group with a sl st or a dc to prevent the braid unravelling.

items.symptom: Braid is pulling the strips unevenly — one side is bunched
items.cause: Pulling the groups through with unequal tension
items.fix: After each interlace, lay the strips flat and make sure the braid centre sits directly between the two strips. Don't pull one side tighter than the other.

content.text: For a bolder braid, use 3 or 4 loops per group instead of 2. To edge the outer loops of a hairpin strip, dc through groups of loops as a finishing row — the same dc-through-all principle as broomstick cluster.
